title: “advisory information” algorithm stops at a shadow root, but all engines walk the flat tree

labels.name: compat
labels.description: Standard is not web compatible or proprietary feature needs standardizing

labels.name: topic: shadow
labels.description: Relates to shadow trees (as defined in DOM)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? The [advisory information](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#advisory-information) algorithm walks up through each element’s parent element: > 1. If the element has a `title` attribute, then return the result of running normalize newlines on its value. > 2. If the element has a parent element, then return the parent element's advisory information. > 3. Return the empty string. A parent element is the element’s parent in the DOM tree — so for a child of a shadow root, there’s none, and the walk ends at the shadow root without ever reaching the host. And content assigned to a slot never gets the advisory information of the slot, or of the slot’s ancestors in the shadow tree. Browsers instead walk the flat tree, from the node under the pointer: - Blink: [`HitTestResult::Title()`](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/layout/hit_test_result.cc) walks `FlatTreeTraversal::Parent()` - WebKit: [`HitTestResult::title()`](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/rendering/HitTestResult.cpp) walks `parentInComposedTree()` - Gecko: [`TooltipTextProvider`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/tooltiptext/TooltipTextProvider.sys.mjs) walks `flattenedTreeParentNode` So a shadow host’s title covers its shadow tree’s content, and the titles of a slot and its ancestors cover the content assigned to that slot. Real case where it matters: GitHub’s `` custom element sets a `title` (e.g., _“Oct 2, 2026, 10:06 PM GMT+9”_) on the host, and renders the relative time (_“yesterday”_) in a `` in its shadow tree. In Gecko, WebKit, and Blink, hovering it shows the full timestamp as a tooltip. Following the spec’s algorithm as currently written would show none. ```html
slotted text
``` Per the spec as currently written, neither the _“shadow text”_ span nor the _“slotted text”_ span has any advisory information. But per all actual engine code, they get _“host title”_ and _“slot title”._ So, step 2 could be updated to say something like: > 2. If the element has a parent node within the flat tree, and that node is an element, then return that element’s advisory information. The spec already uses the flat tree that way for `:hover`, and the language algorithm already crosses a shadow root to its host (_“If the node's parent is a shadow root: Use the language of that shadow root's host.”_). WPT has only the manual [`html/dom/elements/global-attributes/title-manual.html`](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/dom/elements/global-attributes/title-manual.html), with no shadow trees in it — and there’s no way for an automated test to read a tooltip.
